creative_thesis.one_sentence: A quiet, belief-first film that proves, with real product footage, that Navis gives agents and people the same cited, permissioned understanding of a company, and leaves the viewer seeing Navis as the layer between companies, humans and AI agents.
creative_thesis.viewer_takeaway: Navis is building the organizational intelligence layer between companies, humans and AI agents.
creative_thesis.story_spine: BELIEF -> PROBLEM -> PRODUCT -> REAL PROOF -> WHY IT MATTERS -> NEXT -> BRAND
creative_thesis.visual_grammar: DARK = AGENTS. LIGHT = PEOPLE. THE BLUE LINE = NAVIS.
principles: Belief first, proof second, consequence last.
One idea per scene; at most one line of film typography on screen at a time.
Real product footage only. Every product word on screen was produced by the product during recording.
Silence is a tool: three deliberate silences (after 'It doesn't know your company', before 'This is Navis', and the held breath before 'Reply sent').
No effect without a narrative reason (see motion_system.transition_language).
Kanu is a reference for discipline only; no script, sentence, claim or positioning is borrowed.
Every VO statement lands on a visual proof or a deliberate metaphor (shot list maps each phrase to a frame range).
what_the_viewer_should_conclude: They know exactly what works today.
They understand where it can go.
creative_thesis.style_references: Kanu, OpenAI, Anthropic, Linear, Vercel, Figma, strong YC launches — discipline only; no wording, claims, identity or animation borrowed.

hook_candidates.text: AI knows the world. It doesn’t know your company.
hook_candidates.reasoning: Two short, familiar sentences create the gap instantly; 'your company' is exactly what both products serve (agents' context, people's Today). It can be shown with nothing but type, and S03 makes the gap visible.
hook_candidates.risk: Category competitors also use 'knows your company' (Glean/Rovo, per master notes): differentiation must come from the proof beats (work state, sources + freshness, scoping, truthful send) — which the film provides.

hook_candidates.text: The smartest model in the world is new at your company. Every day.
hook_candidates.reasoning: Vivid; maps directly to the Day-2 proof (every session starts new).
hook_candidates.risk: 'Smartest' is a superlative (brand.voice: no superlatives); 'every day' edges toward 'agents remember nothing', which C02 forbids (Claude Code re-injects CLAUDE.md and its own memory). Agent-only — the people product is absent from the hook.

hook_candidates.text: Your agents know the code. They don’t know what your company decided.
hook_candidates.reasoning: Developer-precise; sets up the work-state and context proofs.
hook_candidates.risk: Too narrow for a two-product film (master note); excludes people, so the second half of the film would feel like a second topic.

final_voiceover.text: AI knows the world. It doesn’t know your company. What was decided. Who’s waiting. What’s still open. It lives in inboxes, calendars and people’s heads — so every new session starts with a re-brief. Models will change. Agents will change. What your company knows should persist. This is Navis. For agents, Navis keeps the work state. Close the session tonight. Tomorrow, a fresh one opens with the objective, the decisions it recorded, and what’s still open. You type one word. When the task depends on your company, the agent asks Navis — and gets the facts that bear on it. With sources. With how fresh they are. Every key sees only what it’s allowed to — and only its own company. For people, the same understanding becomes your morning. Who’s waiting on you. The reply, already drafted. You read it. You change a line. You approve it. Navis sends it — and only says sent when Gmail confirms. People and agents, working from one shared understanding of your company. Next: every outcome feeds back into what it knows. Navis. Your company’s intelligence — for your people, and your agents.
final_voiceover.talent_direction: One founder-level voice, close-mic, unhurried (~2.4 words/second), no smile in the voice, no upward inflection on statements. Dry room, no reverb. Speak to one person.

transition_plan.strategy: Absolute timing. transition_plan.overlap_rule: Outgoing scene renders `frames` past its end underneath the incoming scene; the incoming scene draws the visible transition in its first frames (implemented by Transition.tsx useEnterProgress / useExitProgress).

workflow: Clone from 2–5 min of clean founder speech recorded close-mic in a dry room (see adobe_audio_direction.source_recording).
Generate each line separately (L01–L21) — never the whole script at once; 3 takes per line; pick by meaning.
Export the highest-quality uncompressed format available; convert to WAV 48 kHz 24-bit mono; name exactly as file_path.
Place each clip at its start_frame; trim silence so speech ends before hard_latest_end_s.
Regenerate a single line without touching the others when copy or timing changes.
